payout_quote: SEC Fair Fund order (Release No. 105805, June 29, 2026 – Chatham Asset Management): 'The Plan provides for the distribution of the Fair Fund, plus accumulated interest, less taxes, fees, and expenses, to the harmed investors according to the methodology set forth in the Plan.' This returns YOUR OWN lost investment money if you were a harmed investor in that case — it never promises anyone qualifies.
timing: Per-case and slow: a Notice of Proposed Plan of Distribution publishes, comments run ~30 days, the plan is approved, then a claims bar date is set. Distributions often come years after the enforcement action (e.g., 2026 disbursement orders for cases noticed in 2023–2025).
biggest_catch: There is no single SEC claims database you can search by name — each enforcement case has its OWN Fair Fund with its own claims window, eligibility (you must have traded the specific securities during the specific relevant period), and claims bar date. Miss the window and you get nothing; most investors match no case at all.
eligibility: Harmed investors as defined in each case's Plan of Distribution — typically purchasers/acquirers of specific securities during a specific relevant period, excluding defined Excluded Parties. Each plan's notice states who qualifies.
steps: Watch SEC Division of Enforcement releases for cases involving securities you actually traded (e.g., 2026 Fair Fund orders for Chatham Asset Management, Boeing, Barclays).
When a Notice of Proposed Plan of Distribution is published for a case you may fit, get the plan from sec.gov (or by written request to the named SEC contact).
Read the plan's eligibility (relevant period, recognized loss methodology) — if you do not fit, stop.
File your claim with the appointed Fund Administrator before the plan's claims bar date, with trade documentation; denied claims get a chance to cure.
Wait for the disbursement order — payment comes only after claims are processed.
catches: No central searchable claims database — you must match yourself to individual enforcement cases.
Each case has a hard claims bar date; late claims are out.
Eligibility is narrow (specific securities, specific dates) — most investors qualify for nothing.
Distributions take years and are reduced by taxes, fees, and expenses.
Beware of third parties charging to 'recover' SEC funds — claims are filed free with the fund administrator.
notes: Verified 2026-09-22/23: SEC Fair Fund claims are a live mechanism under Rule 1103 of the Commission's Rules on Fair Fund and Disgorgement Plans, with 2026 orders (Chatham Asset Management disbursement June 2026, Boeing March 2026) confirming current activity. In-app, this route must be framed narrowly — 'check whether an SEC case covers securities you traded' — never as a searchable pot of money. No app — sec.gov releases and fund-administrator sites only.

c1.evidence: SEC — the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission — runs the Fair Fund / disgorgement distribution process under Sarbanes-Oxley §308(a) and Rule 1103.

c2.evidence: Official SEC releases (e.g., Release Nos. 105805, 104990, 106073 – 2026) document Notices of Proposed Plans of Distribution, claims processes, and disbursement orders with named fund administrators.

c3.evidence: Filing a Fair Fund claim is free; distributions are reduced only by the plan's stated taxes, fees, and expenses — no upfront participation fee.

c4.evidence: Each plan states its distribution methodology, recognized-loss calculation, and claims bar date in the published Plan of Distribution.

s1.note: Harmed investors per each case's plan (specific securities + relevant period); excluded parties carved out.

s2.note: Free to file; plan-level taxes/fees/expenses reduce distributions.

s3.note: Slow — years from enforcement to disbursement; hard claims bar dates per case.

s4.note: No weasel words on the mechanism — plans state eligibility and methodology explicitly.

s5.note: https://www.sec.gov — official SEC site; 2026 Fair Fund orders confirm the mechanism is live.

s6.note: Steps are concrete: watch enforcement releases, get the plan, verify eligibility, file with the administrator before the bar date.
